   - `{"source":"hostPattern","hostPattern":"^gitlab\\.example\\.com$"}` → allows both `https://gitlab.example.com/tools/plugins.git` and `git@gitlab.example.com:tools/plugins.git`, rejects `gitlab.com`. This is the form BOTH pages prescribe for exactly this case: the bullet one line ABOVE the quoted sentence says "`git`: extracts hostname from the URL (supports both HTTPS and SSH formats)", and `plugins/org.md#allowlist-with-strictknownmarketplaces (was line 771 of the retired plugin-marketplaces page)` says "prefer a `hostPattern` entry over a literal URL so all forms match". The quoted sentence is not evidence that `git` needs its own entry type — it is part of the passage explaining that `hostPattern` IS how `git` sources are admitted.
   - `file`/`directory` → `pathPattern`, which `settings.md` itself defines as "regex pattern matched against the `path` field of `file` and `directory` sources". Measured: an anchored pathPattern admits the doc's own `/usr/local/share/claude/acme-marketplace.json` and `/opt/acme-corp/approved-marketplaces`, and rejects a sibling path.

correctedState:
Accurate but much smaller than filed, and it is a spelling/ergonomics defect rather than a capability gap.

TRUE: `parseManagedMarketplaceEntry` (`packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-marketplace-entries.ts:167-207`) accepts 4 of the 8 source objects `settings.md` lists for `strictKnownMarketplaces`. An administrator who copy-pastes the documented `{"source":"git"|"file"|"directory"|"npm", …}` object gets that entry stripped (visibly, with a reason) and must re-spell it.

FALSE: "that marketplace can never be allowlisted." Measured — the claim's own GitLab example is admitted by `{"source":"url","url":"https://gitlab.example.com/tools/plugins.git"}` (exact raw-string match) and by `{"source":"hostPattern","hostPattern":"^gitlab\\.example\\.com$"}` (both HTTPS and SSH clone forms), the latter being the form both Claude pages recommend for self-hosted GitLab. `file` and `directory` sources are admitted by `pathPattern`, which `settings.md` defines as matching "the `path` field of `file` and `directory` sources". `npm` is not a marketplace source in Claude's own `marketplace add` vocabulary (`plugins/cli-reference.md#plugin-marketplace-add (was line 953 of the retired plugin-marketplaces page)`) and cannot be registered by either product, so its absence blocks nothing.

Failure direction: fail-CLOSED. A stripped entry narrows the allowlist; measured, the marketplace ends up blocked, never admitted. The drop is recorded via `ManagedDropSink`, matching `settings.md:186`'s documented managed-settings tolerance.

The one genuine capability loss, which the claim did not state: `ref`/`path` pinning is expressible only for `github` entries. Measured — a `url` entry admits its repo at ANY ref, so an administrator cannot write Claude's `{"source":"git","url":"…","ref":"production"}` and gets a broader grant than intended. That, not the missing source names, is the row worth filing, and it is small: two extra cases (`git` with ref/path, and `file`/`directory` as exact paths) in the same switch.
